description.purpose: The capability broker: a security boundary made of six cell types and no model. Three messages -- `access.request` -> `access.grant` -> `access.invoke`. A caller that only wants to know WHETHER asks with `check_only: true` and gets a verdict with no grant behind it -- one audit row, no `grants` row, no expiry to sweep. An agent may ask in natural language; what travels on the wire is a HANDLE, and the secret never leaves the connector. `policy` decides deterministically (rules are ROWS, so politics is changed with an insert, and a rule may compare a PATH PREFIX (`scope_match.scope_prefix`) as well as an equality or a wildcard), `invoke` executes and resolves the address out of the GRANT, `sweep` and `clock` retire what expired. Two invariants carry the whole thing: the requester comes from the edge (R-AC-1) and the address comes from the grant (R-AC-2). Since 2.4.0 (ruling R-Policy-Default, 2026-08-28) two of the seeded rows ship ENABLED: colony.mutate.default and affinity.subscribe.default. A freshly instantiated OS has to be able to build and its brains have to be able to register for their own identity, and a default that refused both made the first mutation of every colony an operator step. Both stay narrow -- requester /os/operator/submit, action apply, scoped to /os/orgs -- and code.author.default stays off, which is the line the change does not cross. Changing what a shipped seed GRANTS is behaviour, so it is the second digit (docs/development-rules.md § 4/4a). Since 2.4.2 a SEVENTH row ships and it is switched OFF: `colony.mutate.shell` is the same question one storey up -- `scope_prefix: "/os"`, priority 90 -- because every other shipped row is scoped `/os/orgs` and a declaration whose scope root is the SHELL (registering a template class, for one) could therefore never pass a colony's own front door (GH #514). `/os` is a PATH prefix and thus the SUPERSET of `/os/orgs`; rules are read in priority DESC and the FIRST match wins, so at 90 the shell row is examined after the default at 100 and only ever answers for a scope the narrow row does not reach. It ships disabled because switching it on grants every shell-level topology change with it, and it is switched on with a `seed_rows` manifest (README section `Enabling the shell for the front`) -- applied by the operator, because a manifest scoped at `/os` is exactly what the row makes possible. Shipping a DISABLED row grants nothing, so this is the third digit (docs/development-rules.md § 4/4a). Since 2.4.3 the four rows the submitter asks over name `/os/operator/submit` where they named `/os/submit`: the submitter became an occupant of the front door (GH #556), and a requester the edge can no longer promote is a rule that matches nothing. Re-pointing a shipped row at the node that moved grants nothing new, so it is the third digit (docs/development-rules.md § 4/4a). Since 2.5.0 the broker's six behaviour knobs -- the sweep's schedule, the three page bounds, the usage bound and the TTL ceiling -- and the two SOURCE names of the vault inside it are PARAMS of the cells that read them rather than substitution tokens out of the colony's environment (GH #138, ruling R-0904-6). Two brokers in one colony can therefore be bounded apart, and the manifest that grows one says so with `override_params`, which the mutation door accepts precisely because the key exists under `params` (GH #294). Nothing secret moved: the vault's passphrase is still an environment variable this hive only NAMES (`params.unlock_env`, shipped null), and `key_source` / `credential_name` name a source and a file, never key material.
description.use_when: Once per member or per org level that owns credentials, as a sibling of the agents. Wire the lanes in the same mutation as the add_nodes, at the HIVE path -- never at a cell inside it. The broker is needed where an agent wants a NEW address or a NEW capability -- an answer inside a running conversation stays an ordinary reply edge (ruling L5), so this template is ADDITIVE and never sits in the hot path.
description.not_in_scope: No PLAINTEXT secret ON THE WIRE and no `secrets.db`: `./vault` holds the credentials, and what leaves it is a SEALED BOX -- XChaCha20-Poly1305 under a key derived from an X25519 agreement against an ephemeral public key the requester minted for that one call (GH #421). The message log therefore journals a ciphertext, and the plaintext exists only in the requesting task's RAM. `cred_refs` stays a catalogue of NAMES, and it is the catalogue a grant reads its `cred_ref` out of -- so a payload cannot ask for a credential it was not granted. The older injection at unlock into a connector named in `params.inject_map` is GONE (GH #428): it put a plaintext into the message log -- the thing the sealed delivery was built to stop -- and measurement showed it had never worked, so it was removed rather than repaired. No model anywhere -- nothing here asks one, and nothing here can. No approval lane in v1 (`require_approval` reports `pending` and mints nothing). And no enforcement of its own monopoly beyond the boundary: the substrate has no permission layer, so the broker is exactly as strong as the sentence `there is exactly one edge into the connector, and it comes from the access hive on the connect lane`.
examples: LANES - the hive path is the address and `hop.route` is the port; `params.ports` is empty, so no edge reaches a cell in here. in_request: an edge onto the HIVE carrying access.request as a tool_call turn and promoting the caller to context.requester -- a missing requester is a denial, not a default. in_invoke: the same, carrying access.invoke. grant: out of the hive on hop.route=='grant' -- a handle, never an address. ack: out on hop.route=='ack'. connect: out on hop.route=='connect' into the connector cell -- this MUST be the only edge that reaches it. error: out on hop.route=='error' into a drain the parent MUST wire.

THE VAULT - `./vault` is an interior cell and reachable from nowhere outside: the hive is sealed to its own path, so the port boundary refuses every edge into it from outside the scope. Its `params.broker` is `./invoke`; nobody else is answered at all, and since GH #421 that edge MUST exist -- a vault whose broker is not wired in stays locked, because the topology is what stands in for a signature here. Secrets enter over the user channel only (`meclaw --vault /main/access/vault --vault-add <name>`), which writes straight into the cell's own database with no colony running -- so a credential never becomes a message. They leave as a SEALED BOX on an ordinary invoke: the requester mints an ephemeral X25519 pair, the grant names WHICH credential through its `cred_ref`, and the answer rides the ack lane as ciphertext.

R-AC-1: a body claiming "requester":"agent:someone-else" changes nothing -- the field is never read, and the grant is issued to the identity the edge promoted. A body is model-writable; an edge is colony authority.
R-AC-2: a grant for one chat plus a payload naming another chat sends to the GRANT's chat, drops the key before the connector sees it, and records the attempt in the audit detail.

revocation without an update: one `revoked` row in grant_events, and the next invoke is refused although expires_at is still in the future -- the effective state is the newest event, read with order_by desc limit 1
the TTL: ./invoke compares expires_at on every call, ./sweep writes the `expired` row afterwards -- so the door closes on time even if the clock does not tick

SEEDED POLICY ROWS - seven ship and FIVE are `enabled: 0`. The four the submitter asks over all carry requester `/os/operator/submit`, subject `*` and action `apply`: `colony.mutate.default` (scope_prefix `/os/orgs`, ON since 2.4.0), `affinity.subscribe.default` (`/os/orgs`, ON since 2.4.0), `code.author.default` (`/os/orgs`, OFF) and `colony.mutate.shell` (scope_prefix `/os`, priority 90, OFF since 2.4.2). Ruling R-Policy-Default (2026-08-28): the two that ship ON are the two a colony cannot start without -- a fresh OS has to be able to build and its brains have to be able to register for their own identity. `code.author` stays off, so a manifest carrying a script nobody reviewed is refused on a fresh tree; `colony.mutate.shell` stays off because `/os` is the superset of `/os/orgs` and admits every shell-level change. `affinity.subscribe` answers WHETHER an identity may open its own push lane and cannot answer WHERE the edge points -- a row compares each field of a request against a literal or a wildcard and never two fields of it against each other, so the submitter's gate is what holds the edge to the requester's own hive

CHECK-ONLY - `{"capability":"colony.mutate","subject":"member:alex","resource":{"scope":"/os/orgs/acme"},"check_only":true}` answers `allowed` with an EMPTY grant_id and writes one audit row with outcome `checked`. Nothing lands in `grants` or `grant_events`, because the caller asked WHETHER and not FOR -- and a grant nobody spends is a bearer row with an expiry only `./sweep` ever touches again.
